summary: Settlement posting stopped at ~07:42 because a poison message (orders-3@8841207) repeatedly fails deserialization and blocks its partition, stalling the consumer and collapsing settlement throughput to ~0 req/s while lag grows to ~60k. The fault originates in order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 07:40:00Z), which renamed the OrderExecuted field 'qty'->'quantity' and bumped the event schema to v2. settlement-service still expects schema v1 ('missing required field qty, schema v1 expected, header says v2') and has no schema-compatibility handling, so every v2 event fails and is retried forever as a poison message. The reported consumer poll config change (cfg-3004, max.poll.records 500->200, 07:35) is NOT the root cause: no errors occurred in the 6+ minutes after it, and heartbeats continued. Kafka and ledger-db are healthy. Fix: roll back/forward-compat settlement-service deserializer to accept v2 (or roll back order-service dep-6010), plus add poison-message/DLQ handling and bound the retry loop.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Incompatible OrderExecuted schema v2 from order-service dep-6010 blocks settlement consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 07:40:00Z) introduced an event schema v2 that renamed 'qty' to 'quantity'. settlement-service's deserializer only supports schema v1, so the message at orders-3@8841207 fails with 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'. The consumer retries the same offset forever as a poison message, blocking the partition, so no settlements post and lag grows to ~60k.

causal_chain.claim: dep-6010 renamed qty->quantity and bumped header to v2
producer begins emitting v2 OrderExecuted events
settlement-service deserializer expects v1, fails on v2 message orders-3@8841207
failed offset is retried forever as poison message, blocking the partition
partition blocked -> zero settlements, request_rate collapses, lag grows

assumptions: settlement-service was not separately deployed with v2 support (no settlement-service deployment appears in the window)
the single stuck offset explains the whole-partition stall (only one partition is observed in logs)

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service consumer.max.poll.records change cfg-3004 stalls consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The reported change cfg-3004 (consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 at 07:35) reduced poll batch size and stalled settlement processing. Rejected: no errors occurred in the 6+ minutes after it was applied, heartbeats continued, and the failure signature is a deserialization/schema error, not a poll-throttling one.

causal_chain.claim: processing continues normally for 6+ min with heartbeats, no errors
first failure at 07:42:14Z is a schema deserialize error, not poll-related

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing and error signature contradict it: no failures for 6+ minutes after the config apply, and the observed error is a schema mismatch produced by the order-service deploy, not reduced batch size.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka broker/partition reassignment failure (per historical incidents)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: As in HIST-112/HIST-104, a Kafka partition reassignment/broker issue caused the settlement consumer to lose its assignment and stall. Rejected: kafka under_replicated_partitions was 0 for all buckets and the logs show a specific poisoned offset, not a rebalance/assignment loss.

causal_chain.claim: historical pattern: partition reassignment stalls consumer
current data shows no broker health issue
stall is a single poison offset, not assignment loss

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No supporting telemetry: under_replicated_partitions stayed 0 and the stall is localized to one failing offset rather than a reassignment.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Database/resource exhaustion on settlement-service or ledger-db
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db or settlement-service resource saturation caused zero settlements. Rejected: ledger-db connections and slow queries were flat, and settlement-service cpu rise is a consequence of the retry loop, with no restarts and flat HTTP error rate.

causal_chain.claim: no restarts and flat error_rate argue against exhaustion

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Datastore metrics flat; CPU rise is explained by the infinite retry of the poison message, not by resource exhaustion.

facts.statement: order-service deployment dep-6010 v2.16.0 went live at 07:40:00Z and renamed the OrderExecuted field qty -> quantity, adding schema version header v2.
settlement-service config cfg-3004 (consumer.max.poll.records 500 -> 200) was applied at 07:35:00Z / 07:35:37Z.
The first settlement-service error is a deserialization failure at 07:42:14Z: 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' on message orders-3@8841207.
From 07:44:51Z onward the same message orders-3@8841207 is repeatedly retried as a 'poison message' with 'partition blocked' and unbounded attempt counts (up to 92490).
settlement-service error logs are dominated by 213 deserialize failures and 196 poison-message retries in the 07:00-09:59 window, with error level 409 of 442 entries.
settlement-service request_rate collapsed from ~62 req/s to ~0.4 req/s from the 07:36-07:48 bucket onward (first 60.87, last 0.38).
settlement-service consumer_lag grew from ~47 messages to 61605 (max) across the window, with max 2544 at the 07:36 bucket and steady climb thereafter.
settlement-service error_rate (HTTP 5xx) stayed flat at ~0.21% and restarts stayed 0 throughout, indicating failure is inside the consumer loop, not the HTTP layer or process crashes.
Kafka under_replicated_partitions was 0 across the entire window, so no broker/partition-reassignment failure.
ledger-db connections_active stayed ~61 and slow_queries_per_min ~1 throughout, so the shared datastore was healthy.
settlement-service cpu_pct rose from ~28% to ~70% starting at the 07:36 bucket, consistent with a hot retry loop rather than a pre-existing load problem.
No settlement-service log entries between 07:41:06Z and the first 07:42:14Z error show processing or errors; heartbeats were still ok at 07:36:26Z and 07:41:06Z.

assumptions: settlement-service was not independently deployed with schema-v2 support, since no settlement-service deployment appears in the queried window.
The stuck offset orders-3@8841207 is the direct cause of the partition stall rather than a symptom of a broader Kafka outage.
The observed metric buckets (720s) are fine-grained enough to attribute onset to the deploy at 07:40 rather than the config at 07:35.

timeline.event: order-service deployment dep-6010 v2.16.0 goes live: renames OrderExecuted qty->quantity, schema header v2
First deserialization error: orders-3@8841207 missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)
Same offset becomes a poison message, retried with partition blocked
settlement-service request_rate collapses to ~0.4 req/s; consumer_lag begins sustained climb
consumer_lag reaches ~58846 avg / 61605 max, settlements still not posting

recommended_actions.action: Roll back order-service dep-6010 to v2.15 (or its qty field naming) OR deploy a forward-compatible settlement-service that accepts schema v2 (quantity field).
recommended_actions.rationale: The producer now emits schema v2 while the consumer only understands v1; either side must be made compatible to clear the stall.

recommended_actions.action: Drain/skip the poisoned offset orders-3@8841207 (or move to a DLQ) and reset the consumer to unblock the partition.
recommended_actions.rationale: A single message with unbounded retries is blocking the whole partition; quarantining it restores throughput.

recommended_actions.action: Bound consumer retry attempts and route undeserializable messages to a dead-letter queue instead of infinite in-place retry.
recommended_actions.rationale: Unbounded retry (attempt counts up to 94650) turned one bad message into a full partition outage.

recommended_actions.action: Add schema-registry compatibility checks / consumer-driven contract tests between order-service and settlement-service before rolling out event schema changes.
recommended_actions.rationale: The qty->quantity rename broke a downstream consumer; schema evolution needs enforced compatibility.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on consumer_lag and poison-message retry rate so a stuck partition is detected within minutes instead of ~40.
recommended_actions.rationale: Lag grew for ~40 minutes before being reported; a poison-message metric would have caught it immediately.

data_gaps: No settlement-service deployment appears in the window, so it is assumed (not proven) the consumer was not separately updated for schema v2.
Only partition orders-3 is visible in logs; other partitions' state is not shown, so whether all partitions or only one is blocked is unconfirmed.
The full contents of the v2 OrderExecuted message were not retrievable (logs only show the deserialize error), so the exact field set of v2 is inferred from the deploy summary.
No consumer group / offset-commit or Kafka broker logs were available to independently confirm the partition-blocked interpretation.

findings.statement: settlement-service request_rate fell from ~62 req/s (07:00-07:36) to ~0.4 req/s and stayed there through 09:48 (first 60.87, last 0.38), matching the loss of settlement processing.
settlement-service consumer_lag rose steadily from ~47 to 61605 (max) over the window, e.g. 774 at the 07:36 bucket to 58846 avg / 61605 max at 09:48.
settlement-service HTTP error_rate stayed flat (~0.16 to 0.18, mean 0.21) and restarts stayed 0 for the entire window; the failure is not surfacing as HTTP 5xx or process crash.
Kafka under_replicated_partitions was 0 for every bucket across the window (min 0.0, max 0.0), showing no broker/partition-health problem.
ledger-db was healthy throughout: connections_active ~61 (min 54.8, max 68.58) and slow_queries_per_min ~1 (min 0.4, max 1.62), with no step change at onset.
settlement-service cpu_pct rose from ~28% to ~70% coincident with error onset (07:36 bucket onward), consistent with a hot retry loop rather than a capacity shortage.

Between the config apply at 07:35:37Z and the first error at 07:42:14Z, settlement-service logged ongoing normal heartbeats (07:36:26Z, 07:41:06Z) and no errors; the config change at 07:35 did not immediately break processing.
settlement-service consumes from Kafka (queue-consume) and writes to shared ledger-db, so message deserialization sits on the critical path of the consumer.

The 'schema v1 expected, header says v2' mismatch shows settlement-service's deserializer was compiled for schema v1 while the producer now emits v2 -- i.e. the consumer was not deployed with v2 support, the deployment only happened on order-service.
